resolved_from.keyed_by: the objective in the nosepiece position the plan drives to
resolved_from.note: Six objectives span 20 mm to 0.13 mm, a factor of 150, so one constant is right for one lens and wrong for five. The previous 130 um constant was the 100x Oil value applied to all six. The 40x WI (MRD77400) has a correction collar, so the catalogue quotes 0.16 to 0.2 mm and the store carries both ends. The fallback picks the near end: the true working distance at any collar setting is at least 0.16 mm, so a floor at 0.16 mm never blocks focus, while a floor at 0.2 mm would block it at collar settings below 0.2 mm. That is a policy choice, so it is written here and not in the store.

confirmation.from: Nikon catalogue working distances, held as kb entries objective_mrd70040 / 70170 / 70270 / 71670 / 71970 / 77400
confirmation.note: Catalogue values. Nobody has checked where these lenses actually focus on this bench; carried_over is the honest kind until someone does.

objective_clearance_absolute_min.note: An absolute floor on clearance, independent of which objective is seated. It equals the tightest working distance across the six (100x Oil, MRD71970), so it never binds while the lookup above is right. It catches a looked-up limit that has come out too small: a store value below 130 um, or a missing or corrupt entry. It does not catch a clearance estimate that is itself wrong, such as one computed with the wrong objective after a mis-seated nosepiece. Both limits are minima on clearance, so the LARGER of the two binds.
